articles.title: Plans for New Sports Complex on Heywood Old Road Near Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A new sports complex is proposed for the border of Rochdale and Bury, featuring facilities for Rochdale AFC and community sports.
articles.content_html:
A new sports complex is proposed for a 10.7-hectare site on Heywood Old Road, located on the border of Rochdale and Bury. The development aims to replace the existing Bowlee Community Hub with a modern facility that includes a pavilion, sports pitches, a play area, and a 50-space car park. If approved, the complex will serve as the new training ground for Rochdale AFC, who have recently been promoted to League Two of the English Football League.

The plans include a clubhouse for Rochdale AFC, situated opposite the new pavilion. The revamped community building will feature a community room with a kitchen, a fitness suite, four team changing rooms, and two smaller changing rooms for match officials. Current facilities have been deemed inadequate due to issues such as waterlogging on pitches and outdated changing spaces, according to planning documents.

This initiative is a collaborative effort between Rochdale Borough Council and Rochdale AFC, aimed at creating a Football and Community Wellbeing Hub in Bowlee, Middleton. The proposal is designed to enhance local sports offerings through significant investment in infrastructure and community provisions. It is hoped that the proximity to professional athletes will inspire local youth, following in the footsteps of notable players like Paul Scholes and Keira Walsh, who hail from the area.

The new sports complex will also connect to Bowlee Community Park via footpaths and cycle routes. Additionally, it is located near a proposed housing development of 1,550 homes, known as Simister Bowlee, which is part of a broader plan called the Northern Gateway. This plan aims to build around 7,000 homes and create 20,000 new jobs in the region, alongside improvements to transport infrastructure.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Defeated 3-0 by Newport County in Season Opener
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC faced a disappointing start to the Sky Bet League Two season, losing 3-0 to Newport County on Saturday, August 22, 2026.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC suffered a heavy defeat in their opening match of the Sky Bet League Two season, losing 3-0 to Newport County on Saturday, August 22, 2026.

The match took place at Newport's Rodney Parade, where the home side dominated throughout the game, scoring three goals without reply.

This loss marks a challenging start for Rochdale, who will be looking to regroup and improve in their upcoming fixtures as they aim for a stronger performance this season.

Fans will be hoping for a turnaround in form as the team prepares for their next match, which will be crucial for building momentum in the league.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Returns to Crown Oil Arena for First EFL Home Game in Three Years
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC plays its first home game in the EFL at Crown Oil Arena today, marking a significant return for the club after three years. The venue has been prepared for the occasion, showcasing the National League play-off trophy.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC is set to play its first home game in the English Football League (EFL) in three years today at the Crown Oil Arena. This match marks a significant milestone for the club, which has been preparing for this moment since its return to the league.

The Crown Oil Arena has undergone a spruce-up ahead of the game, with the National League play-off trophy prominently displayed, symbolising the club's recent achievements. Fans are expected to gather in large numbers to support their team during this important fixture.

This homecoming is not just a return to the pitch for the players but also a celebration for the supporters who have been eagerly awaiting this moment. The atmosphere at the arena is likely to be vibrant as the community comes together to cheer on their team.

As the match unfolds, local fans will be keen to see how the team performs in front of a home crowd, with hopes high for a strong start to the season. The club has encouraged supporters to arrive early to enjoy the pre-match festivities and show their support.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Submits Planning Application for Bowlee Development
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC has submitted a planning application for a new development at Bowlee, aiming to enhance facilities for the club and the community.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has submitted a planning application for a new development at Bowlee, as announced on their website on 22 August 2026. The project aims to improve facilities for both the football club and the local community.

Details regarding the specific features of the development have not yet been disclosed, but the club emphasises its commitment to enhancing the experience for fans and local residents.

The planning application will now undergo review by the relevant local authorities, which is crucial for determining the feasibility and potential impact of the proposed development.

Local residents and stakeholders will have the opportunity to provide feedback during the consultation phase following the initial review.
